verdict.rationale: Glama's own docs say a developer can deploy any registry server to Glama and receive a hosted Gateway endpoint with no proxy setup or manual wiring. Calls through that URL are logged, access-controlled and credential-managed, and server pages provide pre-filled config blocks for MCP clients such as Cursor and Claude Desktop. The catalog also lists ready-made remote connectors. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of connecting a client to a hosted Glama URL, and documentation of the endpoint's transport and auth details.

support.subject: As a developer, I can point my MCP-compatible client at a hosted remote server URL and reach downstream tools without deploying any infrastructure

citations.quote: Deploy any server from the registry to Glama and we automatically put the Gateway in front of it. No proxy setup, no manual wiring – the endpoint you get is the Gateway.
Every call through this URL is logged, access-controlled, and credential-managed
each server page shows the exact JSON block to paste, pre-filled for Cursor, Claude Desktop, Claude Code, and VS Code
Search Glama's curated catalog of open-source servers and remote connectors
